# Wildbox — Comprehensive Technical Documentation & Architecture Reference

## Executive Summary
Wildbox is an open-source, self-hosted security operations platform unifying SIEM (Security Information and Event Management), SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response), CSPM (Cloud Security Posture Management), and WAF (Web Application Firewall) into a single cohesive system. Released under the MIT license and created by Fabrizio Salmi, Wildbox is built for sovereign environments requiring zero external telemetry, air-gapped capability, and local LLM integration via Ollama.

## System Architecture

```
                       ┌────────────────────────────┐
                       │   Client / Browser / CLI   │
                       └─────────────┬──────────────┘
                                     │
                                     ▼
                     ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                     │   OpenResty / Ingress Gateway  │
                     │    (Port 80/443 -> 8080/3000)  │
                     └───────────────┬────────────────┘
                                     │
          ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
          ▼                                                     ▼
┌───────────────────────────┐                       ┌─────────────────────────┐
│  open-security-dashboard  │                       │  open-security-gateway  │
│  (Next.js / Tailwind UI)  │                       │   (OpenResty / LuaJIT)  │
└───────────────────────────┘                       └───────────┬─────────────┘
                                                                │
     ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────────────┼────────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                 ▼                     ▼                    ▼
┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐
│   identity   │ │    tools     │ │    agents    │      │  responder   │     │     cspm     │
│  (Port 8001) │ │ (Port 8000)  │ │ (Port 8006)  │      │ (Port 8018)  │     │ (Port 8019)  │
└──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘      └──────┬───────┘     └──────┬───────┘
       │                │                │                     │                    │
       └────────────────┴────────────────┼─────────────────────┴────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                             ┌───────────────────────┐
                             │  open-security-data   │
                             │  (Port 8002 - Ingest) │
                             └───────────┬───────────┘
                                         │
                         ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                         ▼                               ▼
                 ┌───────────────┐               ┌───────────────┐
                 │  PostgreSQL   │               │ Redis Cluster │
                 │  (Port 5432)  │               │  (Port 6379)  │
                 └───────────────┘               └───────────────┘
```

## Microservices Breakdown

### 1. open-security-gateway (Port 8080 / Internal 8000)
- Built on OpenResty (NGINX + LuaJIT) as a high-performance reverse proxy and security enforcer.
- Single unified entrypoint for all external API requests.
- Handles API key verification, rate limiting, route dispatching, plan-based gating, and CORS enforcement.
- Validates Authorization bearer JWT tokens and injects trusted internal headers for downstream services.

### 2. open-security-identity (Port 8001)
- User authentication, password hashing (Argon2 / bcrypt), and JWT issuance.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): Admin, Analyst, Operator, Auditor.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) and audit trails for compliance.

### 3. open-security-tools (Port 8000)
- Containerized execution engine for open-source security tools.
- Network reconnaissance: Nmap, Masscan.
- Vulnerability scanning: Nuclei, Nikto, Trivy.
- DNS & OSINT utilities: WHOIS, Dig, Subfinder.

### 4. open-security-agents (Port 8006)
- Autonomous security agents performing real-time triage.
- Integrates with local LLMs (Ollama with models like llama3, mistral, deepseek-r1) or sovereign OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Log correlation, anomaly classification, and natural language threat summarization.

### 5. open-security-responder (Port 8018)
- Automated SOAR engine executing playbooks upon alert generation.
- Automated actions: IP blocking (iptables, nftables, Cloudflare, AWS Security Groups), user account locking, container quarantine.
- Notification dispatch: Webhooks, Slack, Discord, Matrix, Telegram, Email.

### 6. open-security-cspm (Port 8019)
- Continuous cloud security posture management.
- Evaluates compliance against CIS Benchmarks, NIST, ISO 27001, and SOC 2.
- Multi-cloud asset discovery across AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and on-prem Kubernetes clusters.

### 7. open-security-data (Port 8002)
- High-throughput telemetry ingestion pipeline.
- Accepts Syslog (RFC 5424), CEF, JSON logs, and beats agents.
- Normalizes logs to an internal ECS (Elastic Common Schema) compatible format.

## Deployment & Configuration

### Prerequisites
- Docker Engine 24.0+ & Docker Compose v2.20+
- Minimum: 4 CPU cores, 8 GB RAM, 50 GB SSD storage
- Recommended: 8 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, NVMe storage

### Quickstart
```bash
git clone https://github.com/fabriziosalmi/wildbox.git
cd wildbox
cp .env.example .env
docker-compose up -d
```

### Environment Configuration (.env)
```bash
# General
ENVIRONMENT=production
DOMAIN=wildbox.io

# Security Credentials
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<secure-password>
POSTGRES_USER=wildbox
POSTGRES_DB=wildbox
JWT_SECRET_KEY=<generate-random-32-chars>
API_KEY=<generate-random-32-chars>

# LLM Configuration (Optional Local AI)
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3:8b
```
